Shai Bolton needed flight pay for this huge mark for Fremantle against Geelong. ( Getty Images: Paul Kane)

Fremantle has kept its club record winning streak alive, holding off Geelong in Perth for a nine-point victory that puts the team two games clear at the top.

The Dockers nearly kicked themselves out of the contest in the first half with a string of missed kicks, both set shots and on the run.

They trailed at one point by 28 points, before kicking a seven-goal-to-two third term to take control. The Cats came back, but Fremantle held on to win 14.15 (99) to 14.6 (90).

Ruck/forward Luke Jackson was dominant, with 28 disposals including 15 contested possessions, 28 disposals, five inside 50s, nine score involvements, 25 hitouts and three goals.

In the second quarter Shai Bolton leapt high for a contest on the wing, leveraging off teammate Patrick Voss and a Geelong defender to take a one-handed screamer that sent the home crowd crazy.

The victory gives the Dockers a club-record 13-game win streak.

The Cats were without Bailey Smith, who missed the game with the flu.

Look back on how the action unfolded in our live blog.

Thu 18 Jun 2026 at 11:45pm

By Andrew McGarry

That's the end of the night for us, after a top of the table clash that lived up to the hype.

There was plenty of drama, poor kicking, ridiculous marks and a briliant "premiership quarter" that gave Fremantle control of the game.

Congratulations to Dockers skipper Alex Pearce for his 150th AFL game after a career with more injury setbacks than most.

We will back tomorrow evening for Friday night footy, when the Gold Coast Suns host Hawthorn at Carrara for what is a crucial game for Damien Hardwick's men.

In the meantime, thank you for joining us, I'm Andrew McGarry wishing you all a very good night.

Thu 18 Jun 2026 at 11:36pm

By Andrew McGarry

Star ruckman Luke Jackson has produced yet another match-winning display as Fremantle overcame a 28-point deficit to beat Geelong by nine points and extend their club-record winning run to 13 games.

The Cats led 56-28 midway through the second quarter of Thursday night's blockbuster in Perth as Fremantle's stars faltered badly in front of goal.

But the Dockers eventually found their groove, kicking 10 goals without a miss to go from 3.11 to 13.11 to take a 19-point lead into three-quarter time.

Geelong closed the gap to nine points with five minutes remaining when Jack Henry kicked truly, but Fremantle held their nerve in a thrilling finish to seal the 14.15 (99) to 14.6 (90) win in front of 55,201 fans.

"Amazing," Dockers midfielder Andrew Brayshaw told Fox Sports after the win.

"We played the game in our front half for the first quarter and a bit, but they were capitalising on our errors.

"We had heaps of shots, we just weren't able to finish.

"The message from JL (coach Justin Longmuir) at halftime was keep playing our way and eventually it will turn, and it did."

Jackson finished with 28 disposals, 26 hitouts, six clearances and three goals in a monster effort.

Brayshaw tallied 16 disposals in the third quarter alone on the way to 35 for the match, Jye Amiss kicked 3.4, and 150-game milestone man Alex Pearce took seven intercept marks.

For Geelong — who were missing Bailey Smith and Tom Stewart — Max Holmes was busy with 27 disposals and 597m gained, while Jack Martin kicked three first-quarter goals but none thereafter.

Fremantle's club-extending record 13th win on the trot means the Dockers (13-1) stay a game clear on top of the ladder, while Geelong (9-6) could slip out of the top four by the end of the round.

Martin kicked three goals in the opening quarter and Oliver Wiltshire chipped in with two as Geelong took a 10-point lead into the first break.

The highlight of the term was a huge don't-argue from Fremantle spearhead Patrick Voss on Oisin Mullin on the wing.

Fellow forward Josh Treacy was off-target with 0.2 to go with another set shot that didn't register a score,

Fremantle's kicking woes reached fever pitch in the second quarter as Geelong's lead blew out to 28 points.

Sam Switkowski, Shai Bolton, Hayden Young, Amiss, Murphy Reid and Voss all missed gettable chances, with another snap from Amiss missing everything by 15m.

Even a mark of the year contender from Bolton — who flew over Voss and Jake Kolodjashnij in spectacular fashion — couldn't stop the rot as Geelong kept making Fremantle pay for their misses.

Fremantle's run of seven consecutive behinds was finally ended when Voss picked up the ball from one metre out to slot his second.

The moment sparked a three-goal run from the Dockers, with Treacy's 55m bomb and Jackson's set shot closing the margin to nine points by half-time.

Fremantle snatched the lead early in the third quarter, and although Geelong briefly responded, the Dockers finished with a flurry to take a 19-point lead into the final change.

The Cats pushed hard for victory in the last quarter with the first two goals of the term, but a successful snap from Amiss with nine minutes remaining gave Fremantle enough breathing space.

Thu 18 Jun 2026 at 11:30pm

By Andrew McGarry

Geelong coach Chris Scott has faced the media after his team's loss to Fremantle in Perth.

"I think it looked like two good teams going at each other, challenging each other in different ways," Scott said.

The coach had praise for the opposition, beyond their obvious win-loss record.

"They've (Fremantle) been challenged a few times, they've found a way.

"They're not a one-dimensional team, it's not like they don't have the ability to change it up."

Scott said his team wouldn't be devastated by the loss, however he acknowledged that they had the chance to win the game.

"We couldn't get it done in the end," he said.

"We feel like we're in a spot where we can have a crack at it [the flag]."

Key Event

Thu 18 Jun 2026 at 11:20pm

By Andrew McGarry

We're sorry on a night of a great football match to bring you bad news, but Adelaide Crows legend Tony Modra has been seriously injured in a truck crash in South Australia.

In a statement, SA Police said a 57-year-old man from Waitpinga was taken to hospital on Thursday evening after he crashed his truck into a tree at Back Valley, about 10 kilometres west of Victor Harbor.

We wish him, his family and friends well and hope he can have a full recovery. The Crows full-forward was famous for his huge marks and big goals - he played 165 games for the Crows and the Dockers.

You can read more about it in our story:

Key Event

Thu 18 Jun 2026 at 11:11pm

By Andrew McGarry

Luke Jackson is talking to Fox Footy after that win, and he is very happy - just as you might expect.

"I couldn't have asked for a better night," he said.

"To have an opposition like Geelong, to win by a few (points) at the end, and in front of a home crowd as well."

Jackson said he made a few mistakes in the first half but was happy that he managed to come back from them in the latter stages. We think he is being a bit modest.

They may call him the unicorn, and tonight was a pretty freakish outing for a ruckman.

Jackson had 28 disposals, 15 contested possessions, five inside 50s, nine score involvements, 25 hitouts and three goals. Amazing stuff.

Thu 18 Jun 2026 at 11:02pm

By Andrew McGarry

Is there a stat showing which team hits the post most regularly? It feels like Freo must be up there…

- Tina

Tina,

I'm not sure if there are stats kept on an ongoing basis for posters for the season per team.

There were a few tonight, but it has to be said I do think the frustration levels go through the roof with even one of them in a game, so when there are a few it feels like there is a hundred of them!

Also, between the World Cup and the AFL, the woodwork is getting a rare old workout. There was one (AFL) footy game last weekend where I'm sure the combined total was double tonight's. Sometimes people just leave the accurate kicking boots at home!

Thu 18 Jun 2026 at 10:58pm

By Andrew McGarry

Fremantle kicked 14.15 (not to mention a few out on the full) from 55 inside 50s.

Geelong kicked a solid 14.6 from 44 forward entries, but it wasn't enough.

If the Dockers kicked straighter, it could have been a huge win.

But don't knock the importance of them holding on at home against a fierce opponent. That experience could well pay dividends in a home prelim later in the year.

Key Event

Thu 18 Jun 2026 at 10:46pm

By Andrew McGarry

The siren sounds, and Fremantle holds on to earn their 13th straight victory! What a clash, what a result for the Dockers!

The Freo club song is being roared out by 55,000 fans, the Dockers have a two-game lead at the top of the AFL ladder, and they have taken their revenge on the Cats for their round one loss.

Despite the atrocious kicking early, they managed to stay in touch, and took control with the seven goal to two third term.

If Luke Jackson doesn't get three Brownlow votes for this, there's something amiss. Having said that, Alex Pearce and his intercept marks was an immense performance.

And don't forget Shai Bolton's leap for the skies. It's a good night for Freo, and a frustrating one for Geelong.

Thu 18 Jun 2026 at 10:45pm

By Andrew McGarry

The Dockers are keeping things going, getting downfield.

Shai Bolton kicks it out on the full in the pocket, though. There is a minute left.

Thu 18 Jun 2026 at 10:44pm

By Andrew McGarry

This is like a heavyweight fight, the tackles are ferocious. There is no time on the ball.

It's locked in in Freo's defensive 50. Two and a half to go.

Thu 18 Jun 2026 at 10:41pm

By Andrew McGarry

The Dockers surge downfield, the ball goes to Jye Amiss inside 50 - but his kick hits the post! That could have been the sealer!

Nine points the margin. There are four minutes left.

Thu 18 Jun 2026 at 10:40pm

By Andrew McGarry

It's just flat-out football at this point.

There is no quarter given, and the tackles are fierce.

The Cats wrench it free in the middle, Atkins kicks it long, and Jack Henry takes an incredible contested mark.

He kicks the goal, and it's an eight-point game with just under five minutes on the clock.

Thu 18 Jun 2026 at 10:38pm

By Andrew McGarry

We're in time on in the final term, and everything has to go right for Geelong.

Shannon Neale has just taken an incredible contested mark on the wing. I don't know how he held on to that.

But now his composure slips, and his kick down the line slews off the boot and out on the full.

That's another huge moment.

Thu 18 Jun 2026 at 10:35pm

By Andrew McGarry

What is happening here!

Patrick Voss was paid a free kick in the left forward pocket for an arm chop. His kick was a horror, hitting the belly of the ball. It was two on one in the opposite pocket, but Jye Amiss ran in, put his arms out and it landed firmly in his grasp.

He had to kick from a very dodgy angle ... but his snap was perfect! The Perth Stadium crowd raises the decibel levels, and the lead is out to 15 points!

Huge moment there.

Thu 18 Jun 2026 at 10:32pm

By Andrew McGarry

This is getting tasty in Perth.

Every miss, every error, every slip is having repercussions right now.

The Cats jump on an error on the wing, they go forward, a Geelong player slips as he kicks inbound, but the ball skids wide of the defenders to Ollie Henry, who steps inside and slots the goal.

We're back under 10 points!

Thu 18 Jun 2026 at 10:29pm

By Andrew McGarry

The Dockers take their turn to grab a turnover, the handball game sends it forward, then long to a contest where Mason Cox gets held.

He takes his free, but it's never on line - it goes to the left for a point. A goal right now would be REALLY handy for both sides.

Thu 18 Jun 2026 at 10:26pm

By Andrew McGarry

It's like deja vu...Another turnover, another goal.

This time it's the Dockers who turn it over, the ball is chipped to Patrick Dangerfield, who lobs one inside 50 and Shannon Neale takes the mark.

He goes back, and kicks it! Geelong is back to 13 points behind. Plenty of time.

Thu 18 Jun 2026 at 10:24pm

By Andrew McGarry

The Dockers skipper Alex Pearce took a huge intercept mark on the wing to set up a chance for his side.

Now he's taking big marks at the other end, holding off Geelong.

He took one physical one, and the crowd lost their minds. Pearce cleared the ball, but looked a bit proppy.

Then 30 seconds later the ball came back in, and Pearce leaned back over his head and took a one handed half-grab before pulling it in. Just ridiculous stuff from the skipper.

Thu 18 Jun 2026 at 10:21pm

By Andrew McGarry

It's been a hectic start to the final term, a goal to Freo was overruled because of a push on the line by Josh Treacy.

But then Alex Pearce took a running intercept mark on the left wing, handballed clear to Matthew Johnson, and he kicked wide to the left.
